grants.notes: Union of BOTH install branches, from source. sharp's install script is a fallback chain: `(node install/libvips && node install/dll-copy && prebuild-install) || (node install/can-compile && node-gyp rebuild && node install/dll-copy)`. The left branch downloads a libvips tarball and a prebuilt binary (network) and caches them under the npm cache. The right branch runs only when that fails, and lib/libvips.js:97 shells out to `which brew >/dev/null 2>&1 && brew environment --plain` to locate PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR, after which brew writes its own API cache and bootsnap compile-cache; node-gyp then compiles, using its per-platform cache. Which branch runs depends on whether the download succeeds and whether brew is installed, so no single measurement covers both — hence an override rather than a swept result.

rationale.investigator: source read of sharp@0.32.6 (npm pack), cross-checked against two measured runs
rationale.evidence: package.json scripts.install is a `||` fallback chain; lib/libvips.js:97-102 shells out to `brew environment --plain`; install/libvips.js:164-168 caches the tarball under libvips.cachePath(). Measured twice on darwin-arm64 at write.disk + network, cost 23, 1352 blocked paths including ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/{api,bootsnap}; a separate bare differential on the same machine took the PREBUILT branch instead and wrote zero Homebrew paths, which is why a single sweep cannot settle this package.
